title: Earl Crum's band at Suburban Gardens and Joe Cherniowski
summary: Crum led the band at Suburban Gardens with Hirsch on drums and piano; Cherniowski, Paramount Publix leader, was also involved.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Oh, I asked you about Earl Crum, uh, in different places. Uh, you said the Owls. Now, who, who had the band at Suburban Gardens?
Suburban Gardens? Mm-hmm. Earl did. He was a leader.

But we had, Joe Cherniowski was there. Joseph Cherniowski. He was, he was, uh, Paramount Publix personality leader. He was at the Sanger Theater for a while. Incidentally, and, and he was with Paramount Publix, which he was, he went, in fact, I went to Chicago and put a card in for Chicago to, to, to work with Joe, but, um, I found out that, uh, there was a couple of gangsters up there that, uh, would have taken care of me if I would have gone to work with Joe. And, uh, Joe was at the Chicago Theater. But he, he was at the Bourbon Gardens. He had the band at Suburban Gardens when, uh, when Earl was, when Earl Crum was the leader, manager. Yeah. He was the leader, manager. Earl didn't play with the band. Oh, really? He didn't play with the band. He was strictly the leader, manager. Well that meant you played what instrument? Drums. Drums.
